observationsNotFindings: The naming-versus-authoring split is the substance of this version and it is drawn correctly. OBL-AT-NAMED-CATALOG closes as a naming claim while OBL-AT-FX-AUTHORING stays open as an authoring claim, and the only edit to the latter is one sentence acknowledging the former. A join that had let the naming close bleed into the fixture obligation would have looked like progress and been a real loss.

The FG-3 sentence is the sharpest piece of honesty here. Fifty-one hand-authored fixtures exist from D-106 and it would be easy to present them as satisfying part of the AT corpus. v14's FG-3 rule says hand-authoring is lawful class evidence and 'is not an adapter run', G15 v6 landed that point as a should-fix repair, and this join carries it forward so that DR-103 evidence is not silently counted toward a DR-120 adapter obligation.

OBL-ADAPTER-IMPL is the one obligation with no path forward on this row at all: OD-P1 assigns the concrete packager, toolchain and command line to docs/v2/implementation/ after condition 5 authorizes blueprint work, and condition 5 is structurally last. The join names the reserved tools only to refuse them. That obligation cannot move until the readiness conditions do.

Six of the seven review pins are Claude 2 verdicts and one of those is mine from minutes earlier. DR-120's design standing is accumulating the same single-reviewer character I flagged on DR-112 and DR-122, with the v14 contract pin the one dual-reviewed and recorded anchor. Nothing overstates - each single-reviewer pin says 'Codex not reviewed' - but the aggregate is visible only from the coordinator's position.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no should-fix. The delta is tight: nothing dropped, one new obligation, five object-identical to v1, and one changed by reason text only with its disposition untouched. That untouched disposition is the point - OBL-AT-NAMED-CATALOG closes as a naming claim while OBL-AT-FX-AUTHORING stays open as an authoring claim, so the catalog's arrival does not bleed into the fixture obligation. I confirmed the naming close from live v14 rather than from the verdict that accepted the catalog: the eight rendered classes and the twenty-seven ordered AT-* keys are as the obligation describes, with no aggregate AT-8 key and seventeen AT-ARCHIVE-* members. Two specific claims I chased and both hold. The '51 D-106 fixtures are FG-3' sentence checks on both halves - live corpus v6 carries authoredCount 51 with a 51-element list, and FG-3 is defined in v14 as hand-authoring being lawful class evidence that 'is not an adapter run', a point G15 v6 already landed as a should-fix repair. And namedOpenDecisionsVerbatim omits live v14's owner field, which looked like a mislabelled quotation, but every reproduced string is exact, the field is byte-identical to accepted v1, and the omitted owner content is carried in the obligations. All 15 recordedInputs and thirteen pins recompute, and the live DR-120 row is OPEN as stated. Disclosure the coordinator needs: the AT catalog verdict this join leans on is mine from minutes earlier, and six of seven review pins here are Claude 2 verdicts with only the v14 Codex verdict otherwise, so the evidence under OBL-AT-NAMED-CATALOG is one reviewer's. 20 attacks run, 20 refuted.
